Let  
\[
\widehat\Sigma=S,\qquad \xi=\xi^*,
\]
and define the soft-thresholding operator
\[
\mathcal S_a(x)=\operatorname{sign}(x)(|x|-a)_+.
\]
The tuning parameter in the numerical part is
\[
\lambda=1.2\sqrt{\frac{\log p}{n}}
=1.2\sqrt{\frac{\log 600}{600}}
\approx 0.123906.
\]

The prompt as written does **not** include the actual “given R code” specifying \(\Sigma\), \(\xi^*\), and the exact random generator, so the numerical iteration counts and first 10 components are not uniquely determined from the information shown. I give below the exact derivations and an R implementation which will print the requested quantities once the omitted data-generation code is inserted.

---

## 1) Stationary/KKT condition

The objective is

\[
Q(u)=\frac12 u^\top S u-u^\top \xi+\lambda \|u\|_1 .
\]

Since \(S=\widehat\Sigma\succeq 0\), \(Q\) is convex. By Fermat’s rule for convex functions, \(\widehat u_\lambda\) is optimal iff

\[
0\in S\widehat u_\lambda-\xi+\lambda \partial \|\widehat u_\lambda\|_1.
\]

Equivalently, there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^p\) such that

\[
S\widehat u_\lambda-\xi+\lambda z=0,
\]

where

\[
z_j=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{sign}(\widehat u_{\lambda,j}), & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}\neq 0,\\
\in [-1,1], & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}=0.
\end{cases}
\]

Coordinatewise, writing \(g=S\widehat u_\lambda-\xi\),

\[
\begin{cases}
g_j=-\lambda \operatorname{sign}(\widehat u_{\lambda,j}), & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}\neq 0,\\[4pt]
|g_j|\le \lambda, & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}=0.
\end{cases}
\]

This is the KKT/stationary condition.

---

## 2) Coordinate descent update

Fix all coordinates except \(u_j\). Let the current vector be \(u^0\), and minimize over \(t=u_j\). The objective terms depending on \(t\) are

\[
\frac12 S_{jj}t^2
+t\sum_{k\ne j}S_{jk}u_k^0
-\xi_j t
+\lambda |t|.
\]

Thus we minimize

\[
\frac12 S_{jj}t^2-b_jt+\lambda |t|,
\]

where

\[
b_j=\xi_j-\sum_{k\ne j}S_{jk}u_k^0.
\]

The one-dimensional lasso solution is

\[
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
\frac{\mathcal S_\lambda(b_j)}{S_{jj}}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
\frac{
\mathcal S_\lambda\left(
\xi_j-\sum_{k\ne j}S_{jk}u_k^0
\right)
}{S_{jj}}.
\]

In a cyclic Gauss-Seidel coordinate descent implementation, the most recently updated values are used for the coordinates already visited in the current sweep.

A numerically convenient formula uses the current gradient

\[
g=Su-\xi.
\]

Then

\[
b_j=S_{jj}u_j-g_j,
\]

so the update becomes

\[
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
\frac{\mathcal S_\lambda(S_{jj}u_j-g_j)}{S_{jj}}.
\]

After changing \(u_j\) by \(\Delta=u_j^{\text{new}}-u_j\), update the gradient efficiently as

\[
g\leftarrow g+\Delta S_{\cdot j}.
\]

---

## 3) Proximal gradient update

Let

\[
f(u)=\frac12u^\top S u-u^\top \xi,
\qquad 
\nabla f(u)=Su-\xi.
\]

The proximal gradient step with step size \(\tau>0\) is

\[
u^{+}
=
\operatorname{prox}_{\tau\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}
\left(u^0-\tau(Su^0-\xi)\right).
\]

Since the proximal map of the \(\ell_1\)-norm is coordinatewise soft-thresholding,

\[
u_j^{+}
=
\mathcal S_{\tau\lambda}
\left(
u_j^0-\tau\{(Su^0)_j-\xi_j\}
\right),
\qquad j=1,\dots,p.
\]

So in vector form,

\[
u^{+}
=
\mathcal S_{\tau\lambda}\left(u^0-\tau(Su^0-\xi)\right),
\]

where soft-thresholding is applied coordinatewise.

For convergence of standard proximal gradient, one usually requires

\[
0<\tau\le \frac{1}{L},
\qquad 
L=\lambda_{\max}(S).
\]

---

## 4) R implementation: coordinate descent

The code below assumes the omitted data-generation block defines `X` and `xi.star`.

```r
soft <- function(x, a) {
  sign(x) * pmax(abs(x) - a, 0)
}

objective <- function(S, xi, lam, u) {
  0.5 * drop(crossprod(u, S %*% u)) - sum(u * xi) + lam * sum(abs(u))
}

kkt_check <- function(S, xi, lam, u, zero.tol = 1e-8) {
  g <- drop(S %*% u - xi)
  active <- abs(u) > zero.tol
  
  r.active <- if (any(active)) {
    max(abs(g[active] + lam * sign(u[active])))
  } else {
    0
  }
  
  r.inactive <- if (any(!active)) {
    max(pmax(abs(g[!active]) - lam, 0))
  } else {
    0
  }
  
  list(
    max.KKT.residual = max(r.active, r.inactive),
    active.residual = r.active,
    inactive.residual = r.inactive,
    n.active = sum(active)
  )
}

cd_lasso_precision <- function(S, xi, lam,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 100000,
                               trace.idx = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)
  u <- numeric(p)
  dS <- diag(S)
  
  if (any(dS <= 0)) stop("Some diagonal entries of S are nonpositive.")
  
  # Current gradient g = S u - xi. Initially u = 0.
  g <- -xi
  
  trace <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(trace.idx))
  colnames(trace) <- paste0("j=", trace.idx)
  trace[1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
  
  change <- Inf
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old <- u
    
    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      bj <- dS[j] * u[j] - g[j]
      u.new.j <- soft(bj, lam) / dS[j]
      delta <- u.new.j - u[j]
      
      if (delta != 0) {
        u[j] <- u.new.j
        g <- g + delta * S[, j]
      }
    }
    
    change <- sum(abs(u - u.old))
    trace[it + 1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
    
    if (change < tol) break
  }
  
  if (it == maxit && change >= tol) {
    warning("Coordinate descent reached maxit before convergence.")
  }
  
  list(
    u = u,
    iter = it,
    change = change,
    trace = trace[seq_len(it + 1), , drop = FALSE],
    objective = objective(S, xi, lam, u)
  )
}
```

Run it as follows.

```r
## Insert the problem's supplied data-generation code here.
## It must define X and xi.star.

set.seed(1)
n <- p <- 600
rho <- 0.3

## Example only, if the intended model was AR(1):
## Sigma <- toeplitz(rho^(0:(p - 1)))
## X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p) %*% chol(Sigma)
## xi.star <- ... # must be supplied by the problem

S <- crossprod(X) / n
lambda <- 1.2 * sqrt(log(p) / n)

cat("lambda =", lambda, "\n")

fit.cd <- cd_lasso_precision(S, xi.star, lambda)

cat("\nCoordinate descent\n")
cat("Number of sweeps =", fit.cd$iter, "\n")
cat("Final l1 change =", fit.cd$change, "\n")
cat("Objective =", fit.cd$objective, "\n")
cat("First 10 components:\n")
print(round(fit.cd$u[1:10], 10))

cat("KKT check:\n")
print(kkt_check(S, xi.star, lambda, fit.cd$u))
```

Plot components \(j=2,4,6,8,10\):

```r
matplot(
  0:fit.cd$iter,
  fit.cd$trace,
  type = "l",
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  xlab = "Coordinate descent sweep",
  ylab = "Component value",
  main = "Coordinate descent traces"
)
legend(
  "topright",
  legend = colnames(fit.cd$trace),
  col = seq_len(ncol(fit.cd$trace)),
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n"
)
```

The KKT residual should be close to zero if the algorithm has converged sufficiently.

---

## 5) R implementation: proximal gradient

```r
pg_lasso_precision <- function(S, xi, lam, tau,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 1000000,
                               trace.idx = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)
  u <- numeric(p)
  
  trace <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(trace.idx))
  colnames(trace) <- paste0("j=", trace.idx)
  trace[1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
  
  change <- Inf
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old <- u
    g <- drop(S %*% u - xi)
    u <- soft(u - tau * g, tau * lam)
    
    change <- sum(abs(u - u.old))
    trace[it + 1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
    
    if (change < tol) break
  }
  
  if (it == maxit && change >= tol) {
    warning("Proximal gradient reached maxit before convergence.")
  }
  
  list(
    u = u,
    iter = it,
    change = change,
    trace = trace[seq_len(it + 1), , drop = FALSE],
    objective = objective(S, xi, lam, u)
  )
}
```

Run proximal gradient for the three step sizes.

```r
taus <- c(0.01, 0.005, 0.001)

L <- max(eigen(S, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)
cat("lambda_max(S) =", L, "\n")
cat("1 / lambda_max(S) =", 1 / L, "\n")

fits.pg <- list()

for (tau in taus) {
  fit <- pg_lasso_precision(S, xi.star, lambda, tau)
  fits.pg[[as.character(tau)]] <- fit
  
  cat("\nProximal gradient, tau =", tau, "\n")
  cat("Number of iterations =", fit$iter, "\n")
  cat("Final l1 change =", fit$change, "\n")
  cat("Objective =", fit$objective, "\n")
  cat("First 10 components:\n")
  print(round(fit$u[1:10], 10))
  
  cat("KKT check:\n")
  print(kkt_check(S, xi.star, lambda, fit$u))
  
  matplot(
    0:fit$iter,
    fit$trace,
    type = "l",
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    xlab = "Proximal gradient iteration",
    ylab = "Component value",
    main = paste("Proximal gradient traces, tau =", tau)
  )
  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = colnames(fit$trace),
    col = seq_len(ncol(fit$trace)),
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    bty = "n"
  )
}
```

For all three values of \(\tau\), the final iterate should satisfy the same KKT condition as in part 1. Larger \(\tau\) should generally converge in fewer iterations, provided \(\tau\le 1/\lambda_{\max}(S)\). The three proximal gradient solutions and the coordinate descent solution should agree up to the stopping accuracy.

  }
  
  r.inactive <- if (any(!active)) {
    max(pmax(abs(g[!active]) - lam, 0))
  } else {
    0
  }
  
  list(
    max.KKT.residual = max(r.active, r.inactive),
    active.residual = r.active,
    inactive.residual = r.inactive,
    n.active = sum(active)
  )
}

cd_lasso_precision <- function(S, xi, lam,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 100000,
                               trace.idx = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)
  u <- numeric(p)
  dS <- diag(S)
  
  if (any(dS <= 0)) stop("Some diagonal entries of S are nonpositive.")
  
  # Current gradient g = S u - xi. Initially u = 0.
  g <- -xi
  
  trace <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(trace.idx))
  colnames(trace) <- paste0("j=", trace.idx)
  trace[1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
  
  change <- Inf
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old <- u
    
    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      bj <- dS[j] * u[j] - g[j]
      u.new.j <- soft(bj, lam) / dS[j]
      delta <- u.new.j - u[j]
      
      if (delta != 0) {
        u[j] <- u.new.j
        g <- g + delta * S[, j]
      }
    }
    
    change <- sum(abs(u - u.old))
    trace[it + 1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
    
    if (change < tol) break
  }
  
  if (it == maxit && change >= tol) {
    warning("Coordinate descent reached maxit before convergence.")
  }
  
  list(
    u = u,
    iter = it,
    change = change,
    trace = trace[seq_len(it + 1), , drop = FALSE],
    objective = objective(S, xi, lam, u)
  )
}
```

## 5) R implementation: proximal gradient

```r
pg_lasso_precision <- function(S, xi, lam, tau,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 1000000,
                               trace.idx = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)
  u <- numeric(p)
  
  trace <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(trace.idx))
  colnames(trace) <- paste0("j=", trace.idx)
  trace[1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
  
  change <- Inf
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old <- u
    g <- drop(S %*% u - xi)
    u <- soft(u - tau * g, tau * lam)
    
    change <- sum(abs(u - u.old))
    trace[it + 1, ] <- u[trace.idx]
    
    if (change < tol) break
  }
  
  if (it == maxit && change >= tol) {
    warning("Proximal gradient reached maxit before convergence.")
  }
  
  list(
    u = u,
    iter = it,
    change = change,
    trace = trace[seq_len(it + 1), , drop = FALSE],
    objective = objective(S, xi, lam, u)
  )
}
```

Run proximal gradient for the three step sizes.

```r

  fits.pg[[as.character(tau)]] <- fit

  cat("Final l1 change =", fit$change, "\n")
  cat("Objective =", fit$objective, "\n")
  cat("First 10 components:\n")

  cat("KKT check:\n")
  print(kkt_check(S, xi.star, lambda, fit$u))
  
  matplot(
    0:fit$iter,
    fit$trace,
    type = "l",
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    xlab = "Proximal gradient iteration",
    ylab = "Component value",

    col = seq_len(ncol(fit$trace)),

    bty = "n"
  )
}
```

For all three values of \(\tau\), the final iterate should satisfy the same KKT condition as in part 1. Larger \(\tau\) should generally converge in fewer iterations, provided \(\tau\le 1/\lambda_{\max}(S)\). The three proximal gradient solutions and the coordinate descent solution should agree up to the stopping accuracy.
